title: A batched seeding mode keeps the seeds file from filling the disk
body:
On a large enough query set and target set, the seeding stage writes a seeds file so large that it fills the disk. nail then fails before the alignment stage starts. Runs have reached terabytes of seeds file.

Both seeding paths in `nail/src/pipeline/seed_stage.rs` end the same way. `seed_static` runs `mmseqs prefilter` and `mmseqs align` over the whole query and target databases. `seed_progressive` merges its per-round align dbs into one. Each then runs `mmseqs convertalis` over the whole align db into one text file. `positional_seeds_path` chooses that file, which is `seeds.tsv` in the tmp dir unless `--seeds-out` names it. `Seeds::from_path` then reads the file back in full. `--max-seeds` caps how many seeds `Seeds::from_path` keeps per query, but convertalis has already written every alignment by then.

## Proposal

Add an optional batched seeding mode for very large searches. This is a stopgap until nail drops mmseqs from the pipeline. The goal is to try a few cheap ways to bound the disk nail uses for seeds, and measure each:

- split the queries into batches and run seeding and alignment once per batch, deleting each batch's seeds file before starting the next
- skip convertalis and read seeds straight from the mmseqs align db, which nail already reads with positioned reads for the prefilter db
- cap the alignments mmseqs keeps per query at the align step, so convertalis has less to write

## Open

- which of these bounds disk use without changing results; a batched run should give the same `results.tbl` as an unbatched one, compared sorted
- whether the mode is a flag the user sets, or nail turns it on from the input sizes
- how much a batched run costs in time, since each batch rebuilds or rereads the target database
